state.memo:
# Compliance review

## Feature

Our personal-loan journey shows the loan amount and the monthly instalment, and the borrower taps Accept. The annual percentage rate, the processing fee and the repayment schedule appear on the confirmation screen after acceptance and in the emailed agreement.

## Questions researched

- **q1** Must a Key Fact Statement containing the annual percentage rate, all fees and charges, and the repayment schedule be given to the borrower before the loan contract is executed, and is showing these only after the borrower accepts permissible?
- **q2** Must the annual percentage rate and all-inclusive cost of the loan, including the processing fee, be disclosed to the borrower upfront before acceptance, and in what form?
- **q3** Is the borrower entitled to a cooling-off or look-up period to exit the loan after acceptance, and what happens to the processing fee and repayment if they exit?
- **q4** Must the loan agreement, KFS and the sanction letter be given to the borrower in a particular manner such as email or other digital means, and by when after sanction?
- **q5** Is the borrower's acceptance by a single tap valid explicit consent for the loan terms, and what must be recorded to evidence it?

## Findings (5)

### 1. [HIGH] An NBFC must give every prospective retail borrower a KFS in the standard format before the loan contract is executed. The KFS must include the APR computation sheet and the amortisation schedule, be explained to the borrower, and carry an acknowledgement of understanding. It must also stay valid for at least three working days.

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Show the full KFS, with APR, fees and repayment schedule, before the borrower can tap Accept. Give it a unique proposal number and a validity of at least three working days. Obtain an acknowledgement that the contents were explained and understood. Showing these terms only after acceptance is not permissible.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 29, part 1 of 3, pp. 10-11 (passage 2081)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 29, part 2 of 3, pp. 11-12 (passage 2082)

### 2. [HIGH] The APR must include all charges levied by the NBFC, including fees such as the processing fee. It must be disclosed upfront in the KFS with a computation sheet. The interest rate must be annualised so the borrower knows the exact rate charged.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: Show the APR, computed on the net disbursed amount and inclusive of the processing fee, together with the fee and charges breakdown, in the pre-acceptance KFS. Do not present only the loan amount and the instalment before acceptance.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 29, part 2 of 3, pp. 11-12 (passage 2082)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 6, part 1 of 2, pp. 4-5 (passage 2056)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 24, p. 9 (passage 2076)

### 3. [MEDIUM] For digital loans, the borrower must get an explicit option to exit during a cooling-off period of at least one day by paying the principal and the proportionate APR, without penalty. The NBFC may keep only a reasonable one-time processing fee on exit, and this must be disclosed upfront in the KFS.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Confirm the journey offers an explicit cooling-off exit of at least one day, set in the credit policy. Disclose any retained processing fee in the pre-acceptance KFS, since it is currently shown only after acceptance.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, Para 11, p. 18 (passage 1726)

### 4. [MEDIUM] Digitally signed documents, including the KFS, summary of loan product, sanction letter and terms and conditions, must flow automatically to the borrower's registered and verified email or SMS upon execution of the loan contract. A copy of the loan agreement and all its enclosures must be furnished at the time of sanction or disbursement.

- Question: q4
- Recommendation: Make sure the emailed pack includes the digitally signed KFS, sanction letter and terms, and goes to the registered and verified email or SMS automatically on execution. It must also include the agreement and all its enclosures at sanction or disbursement. This email does not replace the pre-contract KFS.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, Para 9, part 1 of 2, pp. 16-17 (passage 1722)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 14, pp. 7-8 (passage 2066)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 27, p. 10 (passage 2079)

### 5. [MEDIUM] The sanction terms, including the annualised rate of interest, must be conveyed in writing in a language the borrower understands. A KFS must also be given and explained, with an acknowledgement of understanding, before the contract is executed. The passages do not say that a single tap is valid consent, nor what must be recorded as evidence.

- Question: q5
- Recommendation: Do not treat a tap on loan amount and instalment alone as acceptance of the terms. Present the full terms and the KFS acknowledgement before the tap, in the borrower's language. Log the KFS version, the proposal number and a timestamp as an audit trail of acceptance.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 13, p. 7 (passage 2065)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 29, part 1 of 3, pp. 10-11 (passage 2081)

## Research limits reached

- q2: stopped after 4 research turns.

state.memo:
# Compliance review

## Feature

Our collection agents call borrowers with overdue personal loans every evening between 8 pm and 10 pm, when they are most likely to be at home, until the dues are paid.

## Questions researched

- **q1** Do the RBI directions restrict the hours or timing during which recovery agents of an NBFC may contact borrowers, and is calling between 8 pm and 10 pm permitted?
- **q2** Do the RBI directions limit the frequency or persistence of recovery calls, such as calling every evening until dues are paid, or prohibit harassment, intimidation and undue pressure on borrowers?
- **q3** What conduct, identification and training requirements apply to recovery agents or collection agents engaged by an NBFC, including disclosure of identity and the NBFC's responsibility for outsourced collection?
- **q4** Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025 and the Act, on what lawful basis may the NBFC process borrowers' phone numbers and loan data for recovery calls, and what notice or purpose-limitation obligations apply, including sharing data with collection agents as processors?

## Findings (6)

### 1. [HIGH] An NBFC and its agents must not call borrowers for recovery of overdue loans before 8:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m. (this restriction does not apply to microfinance loans).

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Stop recovery calls on personal loans between 8 pm and 10 pm. Restrict calling to 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. and enforce this in the dialler or CRM with hard time-of-day blocks. If any loans are microfinance, check the separate microfinance rule in Para 91, which sets a narrower window of 9 am–6 pm.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 100, pp. 28-29 (passage 2158)

### 2. [HIGH] The NBFC must ensure that it and its agents do not harass or intimidate borrowers in debt collection, including by persistently calling the borrower or bothering borrowers at odd hours.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: Remove the policy of calling every evening until dues are paid. Set a cap on call attempts per day and per week, and keep call logs and monitor them. Define escalation routes other than repeated calls.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 100, pp. 28-29 (passage 2158)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 20, p. 8 (passage 2072)

### 3. [HIGH] The Fair Practices Code bars undue harassment in loan recovery, such as persistently bothering borrowers at odd hours.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: Revise the collection policy and scripts so that late-evening calls are not made. Do not apply any approach that amounts to persistent contact.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 20, p. 8 (passage 2072)

### 4. [MEDIUM] The NBFC must ensure recovery agents are properly trained on handling their responsibilities with care and sensitivity, including hours of calling and privacy of customer information.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: The 8–10 pm calling practice suggests agents are not trained on permitted calling hours. Retrain agents and keep training records covering calling hours and privacy.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 98, p. 28 (passage 2156)

### 5. [MEDIUM] The NBFC must obtain recovery agents' undertaking to abide by the code of conduct. Agents must follow the Fair Practices Code and observe strict customer confidentiality.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Confirm that signed code-of-conduct undertakings are held from all collection agents and that agent contracts and monitoring enforce the permitted calling hours.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 99, p. 28 (passage 2157)

### 6. [LOW] When a recovery agent is assigned or changed after a default, the NBFC must communicate the particulars of the agent authorised to approach the borrower.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Check that borrowers are told the agent's particulars when recovery begins or the agent changes. The passage is truncated, so confirm the full text on the mode of communication.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, Para 9, part 2 of 2, p. 17 (passage 1723)

2084.document_title: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
2084.heading: Chapter III – Responsible Lending Conduct › C. Penal Charges in Loan Accounts
2084.text:
30. An NBFC shall adhere to the following instructions in respect of all the fresh loans
availed from April 1, 2024 onwards. In case of existing loans, the switchover to new
penal charges regime shall be applicable from June 30, 2024. These instructions
shall be applicable to all credit facilities offered by the NBFC but shall not apply to
credit cards, external commercial borrowings, trade credits (rupee / foreign
currency export credit) and structured obligations which are covered under product
specific directions, as also other foreign currency loans.
(1) Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material terms and conditions of loan
contract by the borrower shall be treated as ‘penal charges’ and shall not be levied
in the form of ‘penal interest’ that is added to the rate of interest charged on the
advances. There shall be no capitalisation of penal charges, i.e., no further interest
computed on such charges. However, this will not affect the normal procedures for
compounding of interest in the loan account. Therefore, the NBFC may charge
interest on unpaid interest (including on unpaid EMI) at the contracted rate of
interest till the date of remediation, and not at the penal rate of interest.
Notes:
(i) The material terms and conditions shall be defined, if not already done, as
per the credit policy of the NBFC and they may vary from one category of
loan to another, and also, from lender to lender based on their own
assessment.

state.memo:
# Compliance review

## Feature

When a borrower misses an EMI we add 2% a year to their loan interest rate as penal interest, and the unpaid penalty is added to the principal so that interest accrues on it.

## Questions researched

- **q1** Are NBFCs permitted to levy penal interest as a percentage added to the loan interest rate on a missed EMI, or must it be charged as penal charges without being added to the interest rate?
- **q2** Is it permitted to capitalise unpaid penal charges by adding them to the principal so that interest accrues on them (compounding)?
- **q3** Do the rules require penal charges for non-compliance with loan terms to be reasonable, non-discriminatory and applied on the overdue amount only, and do they cap or require board-approved policy on such charges?
- **q4** What disclosures must the borrower receive about penal charges and the consequences of missed EMIs, in the key facts statement, loan agreement, and the website, and when must they be given?
- **q5** What notice or communication to the borrower is required when penal charges are levied following a missed EMI?

## Findings (5)

### 1. [HIGH] Penalty for non-compliance of material loan terms, including default in repayment, must be levied only as 'penal charges' and not as 'penal interest' added to the rate of interest. No additional component may be added to the interest rate.

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Stop adding 2% p.a. to the loan interest rate on a missed EMI. Replace it with a flat or otherwise reasonable penal charge on the overdue amount under a Board-approved policy. Interest on unpaid EMI may continue only at the contracted rate until remediation.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 1 of 3, pp. 13-14 (passage 2084)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 2 of 3, p. 14 (passage 2085)

### 2. [HIGH] Penal charges must not be capitalised, meaning no further interest may be computed on them. Fresh penal charges must not be levied on earlier outstanding penal charges. Compounding is allowed only under normal procedures for interest in the loan account, not on penalties.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: Remove the logic that adds unpaid penalty to principal. Keep penal charges in a separate ledger head that accrues no interest and attracts no further penal charges.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 2 of 3, p. 14 (passage 2085)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 1 of 3, pp. 13-14 (passage 2084)

### 3. [MEDIUM] Penal charges must be reasonable, commensurate with the non-compliance, non-discriminatory within a product category, and levied only on the amount under default, under a Board-approved policy. No cap is prescribed, but the charges must not be used as a revenue enhancement tool. Charges for individual non-business borrowers must not exceed those for non-individual borrowers.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Confirm a Board-approved penal charges policy exists. Apply the charge to the overdue amount only, not to the whole loan rate. Check that the structure is uniform within a product category and that individual borrowers are not charged more than non-individuals.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 2 of 3, p. 14 (passage 2085)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 3 of 3, pp. 14-15 (passage 2086)

### 4. [MEDIUM] The quantum and reason for penal charges must be disclosed upfront in the loan agreement and the Most Important Terms & Conditions / Key Fact Statement, and also displayed on the NBFC's website under Interest rates and Service Charges. A reference to the website schedule in the sanction letter or loan agreement is not enough.

- Question: q4
- Recommendation: Make sure the KFS and loan agreement state the penal charge amount and the reason in full, before the loan contract is executed. Publish the schedule on the website. Update the disclosures once the penal interest model is replaced.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 3 of 3, pp. 14-15 (passage 2086)

### 5. [MEDIUM] When reminders for non-compliance of loan terms are sent, the applicable penal charges must be communicated. Each instance of levy of penal charges and the reason for it must also be communicated to the borrower.

- Question: q5
- Recommendation: Add the applicable penal charge to missed-EMI reminders. Send a communication each time a charge is levied that gives the amount and the reason. The feature as described does not mention any such communication.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 30, part 3 of 3, pp. 14-15 (passage 2086)

## Research limits reached

- q2: stopped after 4 research turns.
- q5: stopped after 4 research turns.

state.memo:
# Compliance review

## Feature

We charge a 4% foreclosure fee when individual borrowers prepay floating-rate personal loans taken for household expenses.

## Questions researched

- **q1** Are NBFCs permitted to levy foreclosure charges or pre-payment penalties on floating-rate loans sanctioned to individual borrowers for non-business purposes such as household expenses?
- **q2** If a foreclosure fee is not prohibited in this case, what disclosure must be made to the borrower about the fee in the key facts statement, loan agreement and sanction terms before the loan is taken?
- **q3** Are there rules on how charges and penal fees may be levied on borrowers, and do they bar charging changes to existing loans without notice, so a 4% fee must be reasonable, transparent and in line with the board-approved policy?
- **q4** Does the rule on floating-rate loans require that on prepayment the borrower be given the loan closure treatment and information on part or full prepayment without extra charge, including timelines for releasing documents?

## Findings (4)

### 1. [HIGH] An NBFC may not levy pre-payment charges on floating-rate term loans sanctioned to individuals for non-business purposes. This applies to existing loans sanctioned or renewed on or before Dec 31, 2025, and to loans sanctioned or renewed on or after Jan 1, 2026. It holds whatever the source of funds, for part or full prepayment, and with no lock-in period.

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Stop charging the 4% foreclosure fee on floating-rate personal loans to individuals for household or other non-business purposes. Refund fees already levied where the rule applies. Apply the fee only to loan categories that are not covered by the prohibition, and check the loan's rate type at the time of prepayment, since dual/special rate loans depend on whether they are floating then.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 34, part 1 of 2, pp. 17-18 (passage 2091)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 33, p. 17 (passage 2090)

### 2. [HIGH] For existing loans sanctioned or renewed on or before Dec 31, 2025, an NBFC shall not levy pre-payment charges on any floating-rate term loan to individual borrowers for non-business purposes.

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Remove the foreclosure fee from the legacy book of floating-rate non-business personal loans to individuals as well, and review past collections.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 33, p. 17 (passage 2090)

### 3. [MEDIUM] Whether pre-payment charges apply must be clearly disclosed in the sanction letter, the loan agreement and the KFS. Undisclosed pre-payment charges cannot be levied. The KFS format has a line for foreclosure charges, if applicable. The APR includes all charges levied by the NBFC.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: For any loan type where a prepayment fee is still allowed, state it clearly in the sanction letter, loan agreement and KFS (contingent charges, foreclosure charges). Do not charge any fee that was not disclosed. This disclosure does not make the 4% fee permissible on floating-rate non-business individual loans.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 34, part 2 of 2, p. 18 (passage 2092)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Annex I, part 1 of 2, pp. 34-35 (passage 2169)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 29, part 1 of 3, pp. 10-11 (passage 2081)

### 4. [MEDIUM] The NBFC must give notice of any change in terms and conditions, including pre-payment charges and service charges, and make changes in interest rates and charges effective only prospectively. A suitable clause must be in the loan agreement. No fees waived earlier may be levied retrospectively at prepayment.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Confirm the 4% fee was not introduced or increased on existing loans without notice or with retrospective effect, and that the loan agreement carries the prospective-change clause. Confirm that no previously waived fee is charged again at prepayment.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 15, p. 8 (passage 2067)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 34, part 2 of 2, p. 18 (passage 2092)

## Research limits reached

- q4: stopped after 4 research turns.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: An NBFC must release all original movable/immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within 30 days after full repayment or settlement of the loan account.
findings.recommendation: Cut the document return and charge-release timeline from 90 days to a maximum of 30 days after full repayment or settlement, and make sure registered charges are also removed within that period.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: If the NBFC delays releasing documents or filing the charge satisfaction form beyond 30 days and the delay is attributable to it, it must compensate the borrower at ₹5,000 for each day of delay, and must tell the borrower the reasons for the delay. The compensation is without prejudice to the borrower's other rights.
findings.recommendation: Remove the no-payment-for-delay stance. Build a process to communicate reasons for any delay past 30 days and to pay ₹5,000 per day where the delay is attributable to the NBFC. Apply this to all releases falling due on or after December 1, 2023.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: If documents are lost or damaged, the NBFC must help the borrower obtain duplicate or certified copies and bear the costs. It gets an extra 30 days (60 in total), after which the ₹5,000 per day compensation applies.
findings.recommendation: Add a loss/damage procedure covering assistance in obtaining duplicate or certified copies at the NBFC's cost, the 60-day outer limit, and compensation after that.

findings.document: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025
findings.obligation: The borrower must be able to collect the original documents from the branch where the loan was serviced or any other NBFC office where the documents are available, as they prefer. state.memo:
# Compliance review

## Feature

After a home loan is fully repaid, our operations team returns the original property documents within 90 days, and we do not pay anything for delays.

## Questions researched

- **q1** What is the maximum timeline within which an NBFC must release or return original movable or immovable property documents and release registered charges after full repayment or settlement of a loan?
- **q2** Must an NBFC pay compensation to the borrower if it delays returning original property documents or filing charge satisfaction after loan closure, and what is the amount and rate of compensation?
- **q3** Where delay in releasing documents is attributable to reasons beyond the NBFC's control, such as loss or damage of documents, what obligations and extended timelines apply, including duplicate or certified copies and the compensation due?
- **q4** What must an NBFC disclose and communicate to a borrower at loan closure about the timeline, place of collection (any branch) and mode of document return, and in case of death of the borrower, what process applies for legal heirs?
- **q5** Must the NBFC's loan terms, sanction letter or key facts statement and board-approved policy include the document return timeline and compensation for delay, and what grievance redress applies?

## Findings (5)

### 1. [HIGH] An NBFC must release all original movable/immovable property documents and remove charges registered with any registry within 30 days after full repayment or settlement of the loan account.

- Question: q1
- Recommendation: Cut the document return and charge-release timeline from 90 days to a maximum of 30 days after full repayment or settlement, and make sure registered charges are also removed within that period.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 35, p. 18 (passage 2093)

### 2. [HIGH] If the NBFC delays releasing documents or filing the charge satisfaction form beyond 30 days and the delay is attributable to it, it must compensate the borrower at ₹5,000 for each day of delay, and must tell the borrower the reasons for the delay. The compensation is without prejudice to the borrower's other rights.

- Question: q2
- Recommendation: Remove the no-payment-for-delay stance. Build a process to communicate reasons for any delay past 30 days and to pay ₹5,000 per day where the delay is attributable to the NBFC. Apply this to all releases falling due on or after December 1, 2023.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 39, p. 19 (passage 2097)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 41, p. 19 (passage 2099)

### 3. [MEDIUM] If documents are lost or damaged, the NBFC must help the borrower obtain duplicate or certified copies and bear the costs. It gets an extra 30 days (60 in total), after which the ₹5,000 per day compensation applies.

- Question: q3
- Recommendation: Add a loss/damage procedure covering assistance in obtaining duplicate or certified copies at the NBFC's cost, the 60-day outer limit, and compensation after that.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 40, p. 19 (passage 2098)

### 4. [MEDIUM] The borrower must be able to collect the original documents from the branch where the loan was serviced or any other NBFC office where the documents are available, as they prefer. The NBFC must also have a well laid out procedure for returning documents to legal heirs on the death of a borrower, displayed on its website.

- Question: q4
- Recommendation: Confirm that borrowers can choose any office where the documents are held, and that the legal-heir return procedure exists and is published on the website. The feature description mentions neither.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 36, p. 18 (passage 2094)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 38, pp. 18-19 (passage 2096)

### 5. [MEDIUM] The timeline and place of return of original property documents must be stated in loan sanction letters issued on or after December 1, 2023. The NBFC must also keep Board-approved policies, including a grievance redressal mechanism, and the Board must review how that mechanism functions.

- Question: q5
- Recommendation: Ensure the sanction letter states the 30-day timeline and the place of return, and that the Board-approved policies and grievance redress mechanism cover document release and delay compensation. Check that the Board reviews grievance redress periodically.
- Citations:
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 37, p. 18 (passage 2095)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 7, p. 6 (passage 2058)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, A.1 Policies, p. 6 (passage 2059)
  - Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, Para 8, p. 6 (passage 2060)

## Research limits reached

- q3: stopped after 4 research turns.
